name: Rear delt fly
pattern: Horizontal abduction: with the elbows nearly straight, the arms sweep out to the sides and back while the shoulder blades squeeze together.
setup: Hold light dumbbells, hinge at the hips until your chest is nearly parallel to the floor.
Back flat, knees soft, neck long.
Let the arms hang under your shoulders, palms facing each other, elbows slightly bent.

steps.text: Arms hang straight down under your chest.
Sweep the arms out to the sides in a wide arc, leading with the back of the hands.
Stop with the arms level with your back, shoulder blades pulled together.
Lower slowly along the same arc.

cues.cue: Soft, fixed elbow bend; arms move as one long lever.
cues.why: Keeping the elbow still makes it a single-joint shoulder move; the reverse fly works the rear delt more than rows or pulldowns.

cues.cue: Arms out to the sides at shoulder line, not back toward the hips.
cues.why: Horizontal abduction near 90-100° of arm raise gives the highest rear delt and middle trapezius activity.

cues.cue: Finish by squeezing the shoulder blades together, shoulders away from your ears.
cues.why: Prone horizontal abduction with external rotation is one of the best exercises for mid and lower trapezius with low upper-trap use.

cues.cue: Thumbs up or forward for the cuff; palms down to bias the rear delt.
cues.why: Palm-up grips raised infraspinatus and lower trapezius; palm-down raised rear delt and upper trapezius.
Bobbing the trunk throws the weight and loads the lower back.

breathing: Breathe out as you raise, in as you lower.

tempo.note: Raise in 1 second, pause, lower in 2.

mistakes.name: Turns into a row
mistakes.looks: The elbows bend a lot and drive back toward the hips.
mistakes.fix: Lighter weights; keep the elbows nearly straight and move the arms out, not back.
mistakes.why: Bending the elbows shortens the lever and shifts work to the lats and arms.

mistakes.name: Shrugging
mistakes.looks: Shoulders lift toward the ears and the neck tenses.
mistakes.why: Upper trapezius takes over; the aim is mid trapezius and rear delt.

mistakes.name: Swinging the trunk
mistakes.looks: The chest rises with each rep to throw the weights up.
mistakes.fix: Support your chest on an incline bench or use less weight.

safety: Low-back pain: do the fly chest-down on an incline bench or seated at a reverse fly machine.
Shoulder pain: lower the arm line toward 45-70° from the body.

variants.change: Rear-delt row: elbows bend about 90° and pull wide at shoulder height; heavier than the fly.
Arms move diagonally at 45°: between a fly and a high row.
One arm at a time, free hand on a bench.
Palms forward or up: more infraspinatus and lower trapezius.
Cable: tension stays on even when the arms hang.

subtypes.name: Rear-delt row
subtypes.match: delt row|rear delt row|delt horizontal row
subtypes.change: Elbows bend to about 90° and pull out wide at shoulder height; hands finish beside the chest.

subtypes.name: Prone Y, T and incline raise
subtypes.change: Lying face down on a bench or floor; T: arms out to the sides, thumbs up. Y: arms raised overhead at about 120-135° in line with the lower trapezius.

subtypes.name: Reverse fly machine and standing cable
subtypes.match: lever|machine|seated reverse fly|peck|standing.*reverse fly|cross-over|cable standing|cable 45|cable one arm reverse|seated rear lateral|pull apart|pullapart|bed sheet|towel
subtypes.change: Seated or standing tall, arms forward at shoulder height; sweep the arms out to the sides.

metrics.label: Arm height
metrics.good: 75-95 at the top (level with the back)

motion.basis: Top position matches the prone horizontal abduction tested in reinold2004, ekstrom2003 and cools2007 (arm near 90-100°); hand effects from fukunaga2022. Scapular retraction path and upward rotation (about 15-20° at 85-95° of arm raise) estimated from ludewig2009 rhythm. Trunk angle and elbow bend are coaching convention.
